name: flux-env
description: The environment this process got, one record per variable, secrets hidden.
author: takakix2
notes:
The environment this process got, as Flux signals: one record per variable (name, value, list, origin, redacted, hidden), by name. List-like variables (PATH, PYTHONPATH, XDG_DATA_DIRS, ...) come split on the OS's separator. Values of variables whose names say they are secrets are hidden unless --reveal. With names, only those (exit 1 when none is set). Linux, macOS and Windows.

Secrets are guessed from the name only (TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL, APIKEY, PRIVATEKEY anywhere; KEY, PASS, PAT, COOKIE as a word between underscores): a secret under an innocent name is shown. A redacted variable has value and list null. list keeps empty entries (in PATH an empty entry means the current directory); on Windows quoted entries stay whole. origin is Windows only: user, system or user+system when the name is also kept in the registry (HKCU Environment / the machine's Session Manager Environment), process when neither key keeps it (Windows made it at logon like APPDATA and COMPUTERNAME, the parent passed it like ssh's HOME, or a shell set it); null elsewhere. Names starting with = (per-drive current directories on Windows) say hidden: true. Names match case-insensitively on Windows. This is not set: shell variables that were not exported never reach a child process. The library entry (run_with) takes the variables and the OS rules explicitly and never exits the process. The short name is fenvs: fenv is another env tool (crates.io). For the shell's own variables -- unexported ones, arrays, functions -- use flux-set, a builtin of hsh (an external command cannot see them): it writes the same var:observed record, plus shape / elements / attrs and function:observed.
